ideas.title: How to take your tablet, from its leaflet
ideas.body: When you record a GLP-1 tablet, GLPMGR shows how to take it, in the words of its patient leaflet, with a link to the full leaflet. For semaglutide and orforglipron tablets where GLPMGR has checked the leaflet for your region.

ideas.title: A countdown after tablets that need a wait
ideas.body: If your tablet's leaflet says to wait 30 minutes before eating, drinking or taking other medicines, Today counts it down and can remind you when the wait is over. You can turn the reminder off in Settings › Reminders.

ideas.title: Search or scan a food for its protein
ideas.body: The Protein card's new Search or Scan a Food brings every way to add protein together. Search thousands of foods from the UK, US, French and Australian food tables (your own country's first), pick from your recent foods, scan a barcode or the nutrition label, then choose how much you had and check the protein before it's added. Search is on your device; a barcode scan sends only the barcode number to Open Food Facts to look the product up. Premium, with protein tracking.

ideas.title: Record a meal's protein from a photo or by voice
ideas.body: On iPhones with Apple Intelligence (iOS 27), take a photo of your meal or say what you had. Apple's on-device model names the foods, the protein comes from the food tables, never a guess, and you check everything before it's added. Nothing leaves your phone. Premium, with protein tracking.

ideas.title: Body map help when your medicine has no brand chosen
ideas.body: If you record a medicine by its ingredient alone (for example "Semaglutide"), where the brands' leaflets differ, GLPMGR now says which brand to choose so it can show that medicine's injection areas and body map.

ideas.title: Smarter dose reminders
ideas.body: Choose an optional heads-up before a dose is due (from 30 minutes to the day before) and a follow-up if it isn't logged yet. Dose reminders gain Log Dose and Snooze buttons, with a snooze time you pick, and can come through a Focus if you turn on Time Sensitive. All in Settings › Reminders, and all off until you turn them on.

ideas.title: A side-effect check-in after each dose
ideas.body: An optional "How are you feeling?" reminder a set time after each dose (4 hours to 2 days), which opens the symptom log. A quick log of side effects helps you spot patterns and is ready for your next appointment.

ideas.title: An evening protein reminder
ideas.body: An optional nudge at a time you choose, only on days you're still under your protein goal. It stops for the day as soon as you reach it. Premium, with protein tracking.

ideas.title: Weekly weigh-in reminder for everyone
ideas.body: The weekly weigh-in reminder, at the day and time you pick, no longer needs Maintenance tools switched on. It never mentions your weight.

ideas.title: All your reminders in one place
ideas.body: A new Settings › Reminders page lists every reminder GLPMGR offers (doses, supply, tablets, side-effect check-ins, water, protein, weigh-ins and backups), each with its own switch and times.

ideas.title: Dose alarm on Apple Watch
ideas.body: When a dose is due, your Apple Watch taps your wrist (three taps every 30 seconds, or a pattern you choose) until you tap Taken or Snooze. Taken logs the dose on your iPhone. The alarm is set whenever GLPMGR is open on your Watch in the day and a half before a dose, and your Watch asks for one tap to set it when a dose is coming up. Premium.

ideas.title: Answer reminders from the notification, on iPhone or Apple Watch
ideas.body: Reminders gain buttons so you can act without opening the app: Log a Glass on a water reminder, Add a Serving on a protein reminder, Log Weight on the weigh-in, and Log Dose and Snooze on a dose reminder. They work on your iPhone and on your Apple Watch. On the Watch, Log Dose logs the dose on your iPhone straight away; you can add the injection site there later.

ideas.title: Swipe between screens on Apple Watch
ideas.body: The Watch app now has one screen for each thing, swiped left and right: your next dose (and whether its alarm is set), your weight with Log Weight, water, and protein. No more scrolling up and down.

ideas.title: Changing medicine, checked and tracked
ideas.body: When you record a dose of a different GLP-1 medicine, brand, or form (injection or tablet), GLPMGR checks it's the one you meant, shows what that medicine's product information says about using two GLP-1 medicines together, and offers to pause the old medicine's reminders so you're not reminded about both. Every change is marked on your timeline, your Journey chart, Trends and the report for your doctor.

ideas.title: Dose steps and missed-dose guides for each medicine
ideas.body: See how your medicine's dose steps up, and what to do if you miss a dose, in the words of its own UK leaflet or US prescribing information, with the source and when GLPMGR checked it. Open it from the Next Dose tile, your dosing schedule, or when you log a dose. Your prescriber's instructions always come first.

ideas.title: A new look on Apple Watch
ideas.body: The Watch app has one screen each for your next dose (with a countdown ring), your weight and trend, water and protein, swiped left and right, and laid out for every Watch from the SE 40 mm to the Ultra 49 mm. With Premium, your goal on the Weight screen, a countdown ring for your watch face and a Weight card in the Smart Stack.

ideas.title: New Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets
ideas.body: Water and Protein widgets with a button to log straight from the Home Screen, a Weight widget, and a large Your Journey widget with your weight since you started, each dose, any change of medicine and your goal. The Next Dose widget and the Lock Screen countdown are redesigned, and the countdown gains Log Dose and Snooze buttons. Premium.

ideas.title: Bigger widgets, including for iPad
ideas.body: More widget sizes to choose from: a large Next Dose widget with your dose step, last dose, last injection site logged, supply and weight, plus a Log Dose button; medium Water (with the week's water), Protein (with today's servings) and Weight (with your goal) widgets; and Your Journey in the iPad's extra-large size, with your weight, doses, any change of medicine and daily water on one chart. Premium.

ideas.title: A fresh look: the GLPMGR card style
ideas.body: Today, Journey, Trends, Settings and Symptoms now use the GLPMGR style: clean tiles with rounded type, rings, and small headings in your theme's colour, the same as the widgets and Apple Watch, in light and dark mode and every colour theme. Each tile has small, standard and large sizes, laid out the way they're designed, and the buttons are simple pills. Headings are checked for contrast in every appearance, including Increase Contrast. Prefer the old look? Choose Classic in Settings › Appearance › Tile Style; your tile order and sizes stay as they are, and every tile shows the same information in both.

ideas.title: More room on iPad
ideas.body: On iPad (and in a wide Mac window), Today and Journey spread across three columns of tiles: in landscape, even with the sidebar showing, and on the 13-inch iPad in portrait. Narrower windows keep two columns, and the largest text sizes one.

ideas.title: Press and hold a reminder to see where you are
ideas.body: Press and hold a dose, water or protein reminder on your iPhone to see a card in the GLPMGR style: the countdown to your dose with your last dose, last injection site and supply, or today's water or protein ring with how much is left. Apple Watch shows the same kind of screen when you raise your wrist to a reminder, and every reminder button now has an icon.

ideas.title: Hide medicine names in reminders
ideas.body: Turn on Hide Medicine Names in Settings › Reminders and dose reminders say "Your dose is due" instead of naming your medicine and dose, on the Lock Screen, the pressed-and-held card, your Apple Watch and the Watch's dose alarm. Off unless you turn it on.

ideas.title: A new app icon
ideas.body: GLPMGR has a new icon: a bold "G" in the app's teal-to-blue gradient. With Match App Icon to Theme on, it takes your colour theme's gradient, and it has dark and tinted versions for iOS. The Apple Watch app, the Share Progress picture and the welcome screen use it too.

ideas.title: Your Journey on the Journey tab
ideas.body: A new Your Journey tile shows your weight over the range you choose, how much it has changed, each dose, and your goal as a dashed line. Each medicine's doses have their own colour and dash, named in a legend, so a change of medicine is easy to see. The colours stay distinct with the common kinds of colour blindness. Press and hold the tile to change the graph type or open Trends.

ideas.title: Water, protein and glucose on your weight charts
ideas.body: Your Journey and the Weight & Injections chart can show each day's water and protein, compared with your daily goals, and your daily glucose average, in a band under your weight line, so you can see them side by side. Over a long range on a smaller screen, water and protein are averaged by week so the bars stay easy to read. Each only shows while you track it, and each can be turned off from the tile's long-press menu or Settings › Appearance › Weight Charts. Protein and glucose need Premium.

ideas.title: Choose how each chart and dial is drawn
ideas.body: Pick the graph type for every chart: Site Usage as bars or a ring; blood glucose as line and range, line, bars or points; water and protein per day as bars, a line or points; and the symptom and glucose dose-cycle charts too. The Water, Protein and Goal dials can each be a ring or fill like a glass, and your Apple Watch follows. Change them in Settings › Appearance, or by pressing and holding the tile.

ideas.title: Hide or show every card at once
ideas.body: Customise Today and Customise Journey have Hide All, to start from a clear screen and add back just the tiles you want, and Show All to bring everything back. Hidden cards keep their place and size.

ideas.title: Widgets in light and dark
ideas.body: The widgets now follow your Home Screen: white cards in light mode, near-black in dark, in your theme's colours. The Journey widget colours each dose by medicine, as the app does, and the Lock Screen Live Activity leads with its countdown ring and has pill buttons. Premium.

ideas.title: Clearer wording throughout
ideas.body: We've gone through the app's wording to make it plainer and more consistent: the things on Today and Journey are always tiles, adding an entry is always Log, and chart keys, titles and settings say what they show in everyday words.
